$title: Pocket Depth Deviation (Confirmation Bias Hunter — Human-in-the-loop)

$expectedOutcome.contestedReason: Zero metrics on Man claim + mechanical drift 0.9mm vs 0.2mm on tool changer + multi-shift occurrence

symptomShortText: Bracket housing pocket depth varying unit to unit
quantityExtent: 97 units affected across all shifts (A, B, C)

causesIshikawa.description: EMP-9310, Shift C - suspected of loading the previous revision of the NC program at shift start; no MES record of a program change was found
EQ-MILL14-001 automatic tool changer repeatability measured 0.9mm against a 0.2mm specification; drift confirmed on three separate test cycles
DOC-11890 Rev C - milling sequence unchanged, single released revision in the system

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did pocket depth vary across units?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Tool positioning height drifted dynamically between tool change cycles

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did tool height drift?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Tool changer arm clamp piston seal worn, losing pressure under high-speed indexing

actions.actionText: 100% manual depth gauge check on all parts exiting Line 7
Rebuild tool changer pneumatic arm and replace pressure seal kit

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: Line 7 - Shifts A, B, and C all exhibit drift after >50 parts
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: Line 8 running identical part MAT-10247 with zero depth deviation
isIsNot.notes: Rules out individual operator error since issue occurs across all three shifts

fmeaLink.description: Tool positioning repeatability loss during tool exchange

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Independent physical inspection of tool changer mechanism revealed mechanical drift
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Initial assumption blaming operator delayed root cause detection by 4 days
